# Biosirkel studietur-møte zero waste scotland

**Dato:** 2025-12-11
**Type møte:** Eksterne møter
**Status:** Ikke startet
**Prosjekttilknytning:** Biosirkel

## Meeting Overview

Representatives from Norway's Bioserkel (Bio Circle) project met with Zero Waste Scotland to plan a 2-day study visit to Scotland focusing on bioeconomy and circular economy initiatives.

The Norwegian team is interested in learning about Scottish innovations in industrial symbiosis, bioeconomy, and sustainable transitions, particularly in aquaculture and agriculture sectors.

The visit will likely take place in May 2024, bringing approximately 15 Norwegian delegates.

## Areas of Interest for the Norwegian Delegation

- Aquaculture innovations, particularly waste stream valorization and blue-green initiatives (crossovers between agriculture and aquaculture)
- Industrial symbiosis and transition projects, especially those focused on reducing CO2 emissions
- Bioparks and industrial parks with circular economy focus
- Carbon capture, utilization, and management initiatives
- Alternative fish feeds and innovations in aquaculture
- Algae production and applications (for fish feed, nutraceuticals, etc.)
- Anaerobic digestion facilities and biogas projects
- Facilitators and government bodies supporting circular transitions

## Potential Organizations and Sites to Visit

- **Industrial Biotechnology Innovation Centre (IBioC)** and their FlexBio scale-up facilities in Edinburgh
- **Scottish Aquaculture Innovation Centre** and the Institute of Aquaculture at Stirling University
- **Scottish Ocean Cluster** (modeled after Iceland Ocean Cluster)
- **Grangemouth industrial cluster**, which is transitioning from oil refinery to more bio-based industries
  - **MyAlgae** (company using whisky distillation byproducts to grow algae)
  - **Celtic Renewables** (making biofuel from whisky and agricultural byproducts)
- **Carbogenic** in Edinburgh (biochar and biogas)
- **Anaerobic digestion facility** near Stirling (Balfront)
- **C Loop** sustainable biomanufacturing hub at University of Edinburgh
- **Scottish Association for Marine Science (SAMS)** in Oban and associated companies

## Logistics and Timeline

- The visit will be structured as approximately 1.5 days, likely split between Stirling and Edinburgh
- Targeting May 2024, avoiding:
  - Scottish election week (around May 5th)
  - Norway's National Day (May 17th)
- The Scottish team suggested bringing together multiple organizations for roundtable discussions to maximize the visit's value
- Evenings can be used for networking dinners
- Group size will be around 15 participants

## Action Items

- [ ] Stuart and Amanda to draft a 1.5-day itinerary based on the areas of interest discussed
- [ ] Scottish team to send draft itinerary to the Norwegian team before Christmas
- [ ] Both teams to attend follow-up call on January 8th at 2pm UK time/3pm Norway time
- [ ] Both teams to identify any conflicting events in May
- [ ] Both teams to look for relevant Scottish events that could complement the visit
